newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden mourns the loss of Prince Bertil.
newsitem.headline: Sweden mourns the loss of Prince Bertil.

text.p: Sweden's Prince Bertil, whose clandestime 33-year romance with a divorced British actress touched hearts across the world, will be buried after a state funeral on January 13, the royal court announced on Monday.
Bertil, grand old man of the Swedish royal family, died in his sleep on Sunday aged 84, after ailing for several years.
People throughout Sweden paid their respects to the popular royal on Monday, with flags at half mast and queues outside the Royal Palace in Stockholm to sign the official condolence list.
"I think the Swedish people are feeling a common loss and sorrow," Prime Minister Goran Persson told reporters.
A statement from the court said the state funeral would be held on January 13, at 1100 GMT in the palace's chapel.

A funeral procession will then make its way to the royal graveyard at Haga outside Stockholm where Prince Bertil will be buried alongside the former king, Gustav VI Adolf, who died in 1973, and was succeeded by reigning monarch Carl XVI Gustaf.
The king said Bertil's death would be mourned deeply by himself, his wife Queen Sylvia, and his three children.
"Over the course of time Prince Bertil for me and my family was enormously meaningful and dear," he said in a statement released by the palace on Monday.

Prince Bertil, born in February 1912, spent 33 years in the public eye without revealing his love of Briton Lilian Craig for fear of jeopardising the monarchy. He met Lilian in London during World War II while serving as an assistant naval attache.
After his brother and heir Crown Prince Gustaf Adolf died in an air crash in 1947, leaving a very young son, Bertil had to remain a prince to safeguard the royal succession.
That meant he could not marry his sweetheart as marriage to a commoner would compel him to renounce his title.
Under Sweden's complicated rules of succession, the throne could then have fallen vacant if his father, the king, had died while the crown prince's son was still a child.
The couple conducted their affair clandestinely at first, spending most of their time together on the French Riviera.
It was not only in the 1960s that the relationship gradually slipped into the open. Lilian moved to the prince's house in an Stockholm suburb, but never escorted him on official duties.
Their "ordeal", as the prince described it, was not over until 1976, when they married at Drottningholm Castle outside Stockholm. Lilian, who survives the prince, never had children.
